tool_input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(hook): validate the repo root before trusting it for path resolution

Two findings from the re-verification of the repo-root-resolution
round.

MEDIUM: the repo-relative branch trusted envRepoRoot, whose last-resort
fallback (tierBRepoRoot's bare os.Getwd(), pretooluse_dispatch.go) does
no repo-marker validation. With ETHOS_REPO_ROOT unset and the hook's
cwd some subdirectory of the repo rather than its root (e.g.
cwd=<repo>/internal, target <repo>/internal/docs/x.md), the target
resolved against the wrong (too-shallow) base and a relative write_set
entry like docs/** admitted a file it never authorized -- an
admit-widening the resolution fix introduced, since such a target was
always denied before it existed. Fixed by adding allowlistRepoRoot,
which resolves via resolve.FindRepoRoot (the existing ETHOS_REPO_ROOT-
then-.git-marker-walk helper, reused rather than re-derived) instead
of envRepoRoot. FindRepoRoot returns "" rather than an unmarked cwd
when no marker resolves, and pathAllowed's own `repoRoot != ""` guard
already treats that as "skip the repo-relative try" -- restoring
pre-fix behavior rather than widening it. envRepoRoot itself is
untouched; it still backs Tier B mission-store resolution, where a
bare-cwd fallback is safe because a wrong store just fails a
subsequent Load, fail-closed -- a property pathAllowed's comparison
does not share.

MINOR: strings.HasPrefix(rel, "..") also rejected a legal in-repo name
that merely starts with two literal dots (e.g. "/repo/..config" ->
rel "..config"), which shares only its first two bytes with a real
".." traversal escape. Replaced with the standard idiom: rel == ".."
or rel has the "../" (filepath.Separator-joined) prefix.

Tests: TestHandlePreToolUse_RepoRootValidation covers both the
subdirectory-cwd case (resolves against the true .git root, not the
subdirectory) and the no-repo-marker-anywhere case (repo-relative
resolution skipped, raw comparison only). TestPathAllowed_Dot-
DotPrefixedNameNotTreatedAsTraversal pins the dotdot-prefix idiom fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <[redacted-email]>
EOF
)" internal/hook/pretooluse.go internal/hook/pretooluse_test.go

tool_input.message:
Both findings fixed. Commit 28a4377 on fix/spec-backed-enforcement (internal/hook/pretooluse.go + pretooluse_test.go — pretooluse_dispatch.go did not need changes; tierBRepoRoot itself is untouched).

MEDIUM (repo-root fallback): added allowlistRepoRoot(), which resolves via resolve.FindRepoRoot() — the existing ETHOS_REPO_ROOT-then-.git-marker-walk helper — instead of envRepoRoot(). Reused rather than re-derived, per your note. FindRepoRoot returns "" instead of an unmarked cwd when no .git resolves, and pathAllowed's existing `repoRoot != ""` guard already treats that as "skip the repo-relative try" — so an unresolvable root restores pre-fix behavior (raw comparison only) rather than widening admission. envRepoRoot/tierBRepoRoot are unchanged; they still back Tier B mission-store resolution, where the bare-cwd fallback is safe for a different reason (a wrong store just fails Load, fail-closed) that doesn't apply to pathAllowed's comparison.

MINOR (dotdot idiom): replaced `!strings.HasPrefix(rel, "..")` with `rel != ".." && !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))`.

Tests added: TestHandlePreToolUse_RepoRootValidation, two subtests — (1) cwd is a repo subdirectory (<repo>/internal): confirms resolution walks up to the true .git root rather than treating the subdirectory as root, so a target that would falsely match docs/** under the wrong (too-shallow) base is correctly denied; (2) no repo marker anywhere: confirms repo-relative resolution is skipped entirely (raw comparison only, deny) rather than trusting an arbitrary directory. TestPathAllowed_DotDotPrefixedNameNotTreatedAsTraversal pins a legal in-repo name starting with two literal dots ("..config") as admitted, not refused as a traversal escape.
